name: Fleet Foxes
label: Sub Pop
lede: Two Kirkland high school friends, a basement, a Bruegel painting and five-part harmonies that beat everyone to the top of 2008's year-end lists, followed by a drummer who became Father John Misty and a singer who went back to college.

eras.title: The Pineapples from Kirkland
eras.text: Robin Pecknold and Skyler Skjelset grew up on Dylan, Neil Young and Brian Wilson in a Seattle suburb. With no label and no money, they made a debut album in a parents' basement and let Myspace do the rest.

years.h: Robin Pecknold and Skyler Skjelset start a band out of Kirkland
years.p: Lake Washington High School friends Robin Pecknold and Skyler Skjelset form a band with Casey Wescott, Nicholas Peterson and bassist Bryn Lumsden. Pecknold's father Greg had played in '60s Seattle soul band The Fathoms.
years.xp: Pecknold had toured the U.S. in 2005 playing bass in the Seattle band Dolour. Skjelset's mother Peggi raised him on Dylan and Hank Williams.

years.h: The Pineapples become Fleet Foxes
years.p: The band started as The Pineapples until a name clash forced a change. Robin Pecknold liked that Fleet Foxes sounded like some odd English pastime, like fox hunting.

q: It was obvious he had talent coming out of his ass.
years.h: The self-released Fleet Foxes EP, recorded with Phil Ek
years.p: Producer [[Phil Ek|974863b2-1c82-4bb7-b23f-54ddf2713e88]], known for [[Built to Spill|3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0]], helps cut Fleet Foxes' first demo, sold as a self-released EP. By year's end the Seattle Times is praising their lyrics.
years.xp: Ek had met Robin Pecknold years earlier and helped shop the demo to labels.

years.h: Craig Curran replaces Bryn Lumsden on bass
years.p: Before the year is out, Craig Curran takes over bass and harmonies from Bryn Lumsden.

years.h: Recording the debut in Robin Pecknold's parents' basement
years.p: With no label, Fleet Foxes pay for their first album themselves, recording with Phil Ek in Pecknold's parents' basement and Casey Wescott's home, guitar amps set up inside tipis.
years.xp:
It took a year. Pecknold called the sessions constant and exhausting, the band re-recorded the whole album at one point, and he was sick for some vocal takes. They finished in November 2007, with the last vocal overdubs the night before the final mix.

Pecknold wrote in a log cabin his grandfather built in Plain, Washington, and ran up credit card debt that touring later paid off.

years.h: 250,000 Myspace plays in two months
years.p: Word of mouth pushes Fleet Foxes past a quarter-million Myspace plays in two months. Robin Pecknold later credited much of the band's rise to illegal file sharing.

eras.title: Album of the year, almost everywhere
eras.text: Fleet Foxes turned down major-label money for Sub Pop, released an EP and an album two months apart, and ended 2008 on top of Pitchfork, Uncut, The Times and Billboard's critics' lists. Pecknold had half hoped the record would flop.

years.h: Fleet Foxes pick Sub Pop over a major-label bidding war
years.p: Courted by majors, Fleet Foxes sign with Sub Pop, with Bella Union releasing them in the UK. Christian Wargo replaces Craig Curran on bass.

years.h: On tour with Blitzen Trapper, then SXSW
years.p: Fleet Foxes start a spring tour with Blitzen Trapper. Their SXSW set in March gets the European press interested.

years.h: Sun Giant EP, meant as a CD for the merch table
years.p: Fleet Foxes say the Sun Giant EP doesn't show their full ambitions, just something to sell on tour. Pitchfork later shares its album of the year between it and the LP.

years.h: Josh Tillman replaces Nicholas Peterson on drums
years.p: Singer-songwriter [[Josh Tillman|379fb100-063e-4472-b7c2-5bb9eda435ed]], with a string of solo records as J. Tillman, takes over the drums around Fleet Foxes' Sasquatch! festival set.

years.h: Fleet Foxes, under a Bruegel painting
years.p: The debut wears Pieter Bruegel the Elder's 1559 Netherlandish Proverbs on the cover. It debuts at No. 83 selling 8,000 copies, and tops the CMJ radio chart on June 24.
years.xp:
Robin Pecknold liked how the painting looks bucolic until you notice all the strange things going on in it. White Winter Hymnal, he has said, is about friends who abandoned him in high school.

The album later went platinum in both the U.S. and UK and was Bella Union's first gold record.

years.cap: Fleet Foxes (2008), cover: Pieter Bruegel the Elder
years.h: Fleet Foxes top 2008's year-end lists
years.p: Pitchfork, The Times and Billboard's critics all pick Fleet Foxes as the year's best, and Uncut gives it the first-ever Uncut Music Award. Robin Pecknold had hoped it would fail so he could move on.
years.xp: By year's end it had sold about 120,000 copies in North America and 200,000 in Europe, and it topped six of the 17 year-end lists Metacritic tracked. Pecknold's own verdict on all this: disbelief was the only sane reaction.

years.h: Fleet Foxes play Saturday Night Live
years.p: Eight months after their debut, Fleet Foxes are the musical guests on Saturday Night Live.

years.h: Fleet Foxes scrap $60,000 of second-album sessions
years.p: Rehearsals for the second album in a rented house outside Seattle go nowhere. Fleet Foxes throw most of it out, at a cost of $60,000 of their own money.
years.xp: Josh Tillman's solo tours that winter slowed things further. By December Robin Pecknold was describing a less poppy, more groove-based record built around 12-string guitar, citing Roy Harper's Stormcock and Van Morrison's Astral Weeks.

eras.title: Helplessness Blues and the drummer who left
eras.text: The second album cost Pecknold a five-year relationship and a year of sessions in four studios, and it gave Fleet Foxes their highest chart peak. It also ended with their drummer walking out to become Father John Misty.

years.h: Morgan Henderson of The Blood Brothers joins Fleet Foxes
years.p: Former [[The Blood Brothers|b847568f-cd75-44c7-b87b-4f38a5a9f661]] bassist Morgan Henderson joins on upright bass and woodwinds, making Fleet Foxes a six-piece for Helplessness Blues.
years.xp: Sessions ran from January to December 2010 across Reciprocal Recording and Avast in Seattle, Bear Creek in Woodinville and Dreamland in West Hurley, New York. Robin Pecknold's girlfriend of five years left over the strain the album put on them; they tried again once she heard it, then split for good.

years.h: "Helplessness Blues" goes out as a free download
years.p: Fleet Foxes preview the second album by giving away its title track.

years.h: Helplessness Blues reaches No. 4
years.p: Fleet Foxes' second album is their highest chart peak on the Billboard 200. The cover is by Seattle artist Toby Liebowitz, painted by Christopher Alderson.

years.h: Sean Pecknold's video for "The Shrine / An Argument"
years.p: Robin Pecknold's brother Sean, the band's go-to director, releases the video for the album's eight-minute centerpiece.

years.big: The drummer leaves. Father John Misty arrives.
years.h: Josh Tillman quits Fleet Foxes and becomes Father John Misty
years.p: Josh Tillman plays his last Fleet Foxes show in Tokyo on January 20, 2012, moves to Los Angeles and releases Fear Fun as [[Father John Misty|172053e5-a7fb-4548-a64d-c53858b5e775]] on Sub Pop that May.
years.xp: In an October 2020 Reddit AMA, Robin Pecknold said Tillman had really quit after recording his drums, and that Sub Pop would only release Tillman's album if he waited a year to tour Helplessness Blues. Pecknold said that tour involved substance abuse, sabotaged shows, ill treatment and trash talk, while the band paid Tillman for songs he hadn't worked on.

years.h: Helplessness Blues is up for a Grammy
years.p: Fleet Foxes are nominated for Best Folk Album at the 54th Grammy Awards.

eras.title: Step one, step two, then Columbia
eras.text: Fleet Foxes went quiet, and their singer went to college in New York. Two cryptic Facebook posts and a leaked iTunes screenshot were all fans had to go on.

years.h: "Step one", "Step two": two Fleet Foxes posts, then gone
years.p: Fleet Foxes post a photo of a laptop, microphone and guitar captioned Step one, and the next day a broken mandolin captioned Step two. Both are deleted.

years.h: Robin Pecknold goes to Columbia University
years.p: Robin Pecknold announces he has moved to New York for an undergraduate degree at Columbia's School of General Studies. He studies English.
years.xp: He left in 2016 to tour with [[Joanna Newsom|cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c]] and, as of 2022, hadn't finished the degree.

years.h: Fleet Foxes are back at work with drummer Neal Morgan
years.p: On Instagram Robin Pecknold says new songs are underway with Neal Morgan, drummer for Joanna Newsom and [[Bill Callahan|c309d914-93af-4b3f-8058-d79c75ea89da]]. The core is now a five-piece, with drummers brought in as needed.

years.h: An iTunes screenshot leaks an album called Ylajali
years.p: Robin Pecknold posts an iTunes queue with an unknown album, Ylajali, and a Nonesuch logo. Fans trace the name to Knut Hamsun's novel Hunger.

eras.title: Crack-Up
eras.text: Six years after their last album, Fleet Foxes came back on a new label with a long, knotty record named after an F. Scott Fitzgerald essay, and a drummer from The Walkmen.

years.h: Fleet Foxes announce Crack-Up on Nonesuch
years.p: The third album gets a name, a new label and a nine-minute first single, Third of May / Ōdaigahara.

years.h: Fleet Foxes return live at the Wilma in Missoula
years.p: Fleet Foxes' first show in years runs through nine new songs plus a Bee Gees cover, In the Morning, with [[Matt Barrick|ebba7a50-23fc-412d-9451-a9ac183b31b7]] of [[The Walkmen|b7834ebd-64ae-46c3-a930-2d3a52ee743a]] on drums.

years.h: Crack-Up, named for F. Scott Fitzgerald's essay
years.p: Recorded at Electric Lady and Sear Sound in New York with three drummers and brass quartet The Westerlies.

years.h: "Crack-Up" rearranged for an Icelandic women's choir
years.p: For Record Store Day, Fleet Foxes release a choral version of Crack-Up with Iceland's Graduale Nobili.

eras.title: Shore, released on the equinox
eras.text: Pecknold made the fourth album nearly alone, through anxiety and a pandemic, and dropped it with a day's notice. Since then Fleet Foxes have lived on solstices, equinoxes and solo acoustic nights.

years.h: Robin Pecknold's lockdown drives finish the lyrics for Shore
years.p: With lyrics unfinished, Robin Pecknold's anxiety spikes. Stuck in Greenwich Village in lockdown, he takes day-long drives to Lake Minnewaska and writes his way out.
years.xp: Pecknold said the pandemic made the anxiety disappear and put the music's importance in perspective. To finish fast, he made the album without Skyler Skjelset, Casey Wescott, Christian Wargo or Morgan Henderson, working with engineer Beatriz Artola.

years.h: Shore drops at 9:31 a.m. ET, on the autumn equinox
years.p: Announced one day ahead on Anti-, Shore arrives with a 55-minute Super 16mm film by Kersti Jan Werdal. Sunblind names dead heroes from Elliott Smith and David Berman to former Shin [[Richard Swift|dd5f8909-245d-458b-833a-cd6b698399ce]].
years.xp: Guests include Uwade Akhere, Tim Bernardes and Grizzly Bear's Christopher Bear and Daniel Rossen. Pecknold described the theme as life in the face of death.

years.h: A Very Lonely Solstice from a Brooklyn church
years.p: Robin Pecknold plays a solo livestream on the winter solstice inside St. Ann & the Holy Trinity Church in Brooklyn, dedicated to Sam Jayne of [[Love as Laughter|8f5c6093-27ba-402d-b092-4157c93a4104]]. It comes out as a live album a year later.

years.h: Shore gets a Grammy nomination
years.p: Fleet Foxes' fourth album is nominated for Best Alternative Music Album at the 64th Grammys.

years.h: Fleet Foxes stream an equinox show from Boston Harbor
years.p: On Shore's second birthday, Fleet Foxes play Leader Bank Pavilion in Boston for a livestream, released as Live on Boston Harbor on YouTube that December. Christopher Icasiano is now the band's drummer.

years.h: Robin Pecknold books solo acoustic nights in the Northeast
years.p: Robin Pecknold announces four April 2026 solo acoustic shows at Northeast performing arts centers: Fleet Foxes songs, covers and rarities.
